question.text: Kavya invests Rs.10,00,000 in an equity scheme. After stamp duty deduction, how many units will she receive if the applicable NAV is Rs.25.00?

explanation.text: The Logic: Stamp duty on mutual fund purchases is 0.005% (p.150). Stamp duty = 0.005% of Rs.10,00,000 = Rs.50. Net investment = Rs.10,00,000 - Rs.50 = Rs.9,99,950. Units = Rs.9,99,950 / Rs.25.00 = 39,998 units. The Trap: Without stamp duty, Kavya would get 40,000 units. The Rs.50 stamp duty reduces her allotment by exactly 2 units. The 39,980 figure incorrectly assumes a much larger stamp-duty deduction of Rs.500, which is ten times the correct 0.005% rate. Note: Stamp duty applies to mutual fund purchases (including SIPs, switch-ins and dividend reinvestments) at 0.005% of the investment amount. RTAs deduct stamp duty before computing unit allotment, as supported by pages 94 and 150 of the NISM Series II-B workbook.
